title: Telling sounds apart
keyIdea: Every thing makes its own sound. A dog goes woof. A tap goes drip. If you listen well, you can tell what made a sound without looking. You can tell if two sounds are the same or not. Looks and size do not tell you the sound: you have to listen.
familyTip: Play the eyes-shut game. Your child closes their eyes while you make a sound: shake keys, run the tap, knock on the door. Can they tell you what it was? Make two shakers from pots of rice and pasta and ask: same or different? On a walk, stop and ask: what can we hear?

visual.caption: Who makes this sound: an animal, or a thing at home? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name hidden sounds, match shakers by ear, say same or different, sort loud and quiet, go on a sound walk.

kid: Shut your eyes. Listen. Woof woof! What made that sound? A dog! You did not see it. Your ears told you.
Every thing has its own sound. A cow says moo. A drum goes boom. A clock goes tick tock. The tap goes drip drip.
Some sounds are the same. Some are not. Woof and woof are the same. Moo and baa are not. Ring ring and ding dong are close, but not the same.
Do not look. Listen! Two red shakers can sound different. A big elephant can be quiet. A tiny baby can be very loud.
adult: Ages 2 to 3. This is general sound discrimination, Aspect 1 of Phase 1 in Letters and Sounds (DfES 2007), with a taste of Aspect 2, instrumental sounds. Development Matters (2021) lists it under Communication and Language: listening, attention and understanding. It builds the ear that later hears phonemes in words. Key words: auditory discrimination, environmental sounds, sound source, same and different, loud and quiet.

At this age, children learn this by playing with real sounds. Go on a listening walk. Play the eyes-shut game with keys, a tap or a door. Make shakers from pots filled with rice, pasta or bells, and match them in pairs. Keep it short and fun, and name the sound and the thing that made it.

Common mistakes: matching shakers by colour instead of sound; thinking big things are loud and small things are quiet; saying two sounds are the same because the two things are the same kind (both toys, both animals); and mixing up close sounds such as a phone and a doorbell. Each one is fixed the same way: stop, listen again, then decide.

In the lab your child hears a sound with the picture hidden and picks who made it. They shake six shakers whose colours do not match what is inside and find the 3 pairs by ear. They judge six pairs of sounds as same or different, sort loud from quiet when size is the trap, and find five sounds on a walk round the house.

practice.prompt: Shut your eyes. Moo! Who made that sound?
practice.hint: Which animal says moo? A sheep says baa.
practice.explain: A cow says moo. You knew it with your ears, not your eyes.

practice.prompt: You hear a drum go boom {n} times, then boom {n} times again. Same or different?
practice.hint: Both times it was boom, boom from the drum. Was anything new?
practice.explain: It was the drum both times, {n} booms each time. So the sounds are the same.

practice.prompt: Two shakers are both blue. Will they sound the same?
choices: Yes, blue ones are always loud
practice.hint: Does the colour make the sound, or what is inside?
practice.explain: The sound comes from what is inside. Shake them both and listen.

practice.prompt: The clock goes tick tock. You count {n} ticks. Is the clock loud or quiet?
practice.hint: Do you have to listen hard to hear a clock tick?
practice.explain: A clock tick is quiet. You have to listen hard to hear all {n} ticks.

practice.prompt: Knock knock! What made that sound?
practice.hint: The tap goes drip drip. The bath goes splash. What goes knock knock?
practice.explain: Someone is at the door. Knock knock is the door.

pool.prompt: Quack quack! Who made that sound?
pool.hint: A hen says cluck. A dog says woof. Who says quack?
pool.explain: A duck says quack quack. Each animal has its own sound.

pool.prompt: Moo, then baa. Same or different?
pool.hint: Say them out loud: moo, baa. Do they sound alike?
pool.explain: Moo is a cow and baa is a sheep. The sounds are different.

pool.prompt: A tiny baby is crying. Is it loud or quiet?
pool.hint: Does a small thing always make a small sound?
pool.explain: A baby is small, but crying is very loud. Size does not tell you the sound.

pool.prompt: Drip, drip, drip. What made that sound?
pool.hint: The phone rings. The clock ticks. What drips?
pool.explain: Drip drip is water from the tap.

pool.prompt: {n} shakers have rice inside. They are all different colours. Do they sound the same?
pool.hint: What makes the sound: the colour or the rice?
pool.explain: All {n} have rice inside, so they all go shh shh. Colour does not change the sound.

pool.prompt: A big elephant walks on tiptoe. Loud or quiet?
pool.hint: How do your feet sound when you tiptoe?
pool.explain: Tiptoeing is quiet, even for a big elephant. Listen, do not guess from size.

pool.prompt: Ring ring, then ding dong. Same or different?
pool.hint: They are close. Listen again. Which one is the doorbell?
pool.explain: Ring ring is a phone. Ding dong is a doorbell. Close, but different.

pool.prompt: Boom boom, then shh shh. Both are toys. Same or different?
pool.hint: Do not think about what they are. Listen to how they sound.
pool.explain: Boom is a drum and shh is a shaker. Both are toys, but the sounds are different.

pool.prompt: You hear woof woof {n} times. Who is it?
pool.hint: Which one barks? A cat says meow.
pool.explain: Woof woof is a dog, even if it barks {n} times.
